EPIDEMIOLOGY II · READINGS
:::
# Core readings
## Read methods to understand assumptions, not to collect citations.
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
## Essential
- Hernán MA, Robins JM. *Causal Inference: What If*. Use Part I for causal effects, exchangeability, positivity and DAG logic; Part II for standardisation, IP weighting and g-methods; Part III for longitudinal treatment strategies.
- Lash TL, VanderWeele TJ, Haneuse S, Rothman KJ, eds. *Modern Epidemiology*, 4th ed. Use as a reference for design, selection, confounding, measurement error and advanced effect interpretation.
- Current STROBE guidance for transparent reporting of observational studies.
- CONSORT 2025 for randomised-trial reporting; it supersedes CONSORT 2010.
- STARD 2015 for diagnostic-accuracy studies.
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
## Target-trial and longitudinal causal inference
Read target-trial emulation papers alongside practical examples. Focus on eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, time zero, follow-up, outcome, estimand and analysis—not on treating the phrase “target trial” as a quality label.
:::
::: {.lipps-section}
## Reading discipline
For each methods paper, record:
1. the causal estimand;
2. identification assumptions;
3. estimator;
4. required data structure;
5. diagnostics;
6. common violations;
7. what sensitivity analysis would be informative.
:::
